==Problem==
A donkey suffers an attack of hiccups and the first hiccup happens at <imath>4:00</imath> one afternoon. Suppose that
the donkey hiccups regularly every <imath>5</imath> seconds. At what time does the donkey’s <imath>700</imath>th hiccup occur?

<imath>\textbf{(A) }15 \text{ seconds after } 4:58</imath>

<imath>\textbf{(B) }20 \text{ seconds after } 4:58</imath>

<imath>\textbf{(C) }25 \text{ seconds after } 4:58</imath>

<imath>\textbf{(D) }30 \text{ seconds after } 4:58</imath>

<imath>\textbf{(E) }35 \text{ seconds after } 4:58</imath>

==Solution 1==

Since the donkey hiccupped the 1st hiccup at <imath>4:00</imath>, it hiccupped for <imath>5 \cdot (700-1) = 3495</imath> seconds, which is <imath>58</imath> minutes and <imath>15</imath> seconds, so the answer is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(A) }15 \text{ seconds after } 4:58}</imath>.

~MrThinker

==Solution 2 (Faster)==

We see that the minute has already been determined.
The donkey hiccups once every 5 seconds, or 12 times a minute. <imath>700\equiv 4 \pmod{12}</imath>, so the 700th hiccup happened on the same second as the 4th, which occurred on the <imath>5(4-1)=15</imath>th second. <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(A) }15 \text{ seconds after } 4:58}</imath>.

~not_slay and HIPHOPFROG1

==Solution 3 (Another Fast Way)==

We can add <imath>7\cdot500=3500</imath> and then minus <imath>5</imath> seconds.
<cmath>\begin{align*}
4:00+3500\text{ seconds} &= 4:00+3600\text{ seconds }-100\text{ seconds} \\
&=4:00+1\text{ hour }-100\text{ seconds} \\
&=5:00-100\text{ seconds} \\
&=20 \text{ seconds after } 4:58.
\end{align*}</cmath>
Finally, we minus <imath>5</imath> seconds giving <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(A) }15 \text{ seconds after } 4:58}</imath>.

~Pancakerunner2
